I wanted to give this plain front yard a premium upgrade, so I grabbed my tools and got to work! Watching the real progress unfold in this timelapse is incredibly satisfying. Here is a step-by-step breakdown of how I built this modern rock garden: 1️⃣ First, I mapped out a smooth, curved border on the grass using white spray paint. 2️⃣ Next, I dug out the edge along the line and laid down a heavy-duty black weed barrier. 3️⃣ I installed a sleek stone border, block by block, to keep everything neat and contained. 4️⃣ Then came the best part—pouring and leveling tons of crisp white river rocks for that beautiful, high-contrast look. 5️⃣ Finally, I styled the space by placing a dark statement sphere, planting some architectural agaves, and adding solar pathway lights. Seeing the before and after of this build progress makes all the hard work totally worth it! Step by step instructions ⬇️ Supplies Needed:  Spray paint, shovel, rake, work gloves, hand tamper/plate compactor, weed barrier, paver sand, your chosen pavers (we used 24”x16”), level, plastic edging & stakes, hammer, utility knife, wheelbarrow, tape measure, white marble rock, Dominator Mulch Glue, garden sprayer, and Dominator Wet Look Paver Sealer. Here’s how ya do it: ➡️Clear and roughly level your area, ensuring a slight slope for drainage. Compact the soil thoroughly. Mark your walkway's perimeter with spray paint (ours is 48” wide!), then install plastic paver edging firmly along your lines. ➡️Lay down landscape weed barrier and secure it with stakes. Spread 1-2 inches of paver sand, smoothing it out (don't compact yet!). Start laying your pavers, maintaining consistent spacing (we used an 11-inch gap between our 24”x16” pavers, using a 24”x11” styrofoam guide). Gently tap each paver level with a rubber mallet, adding sand underneath if needed. For extra stability, we nailed two plastic edging stakes on each side of every paver. ➡️Spread your rock evenly around the pavers, (ours vary in size from 1/2”- 2”) making sure it's level with the paver tops. Rinse and wash all dust and dirt from the rocks and pavers – let them dry completely! Then, spray Dominator Mulch Glue generously over the marble rock (undiluted, up to 3 coats or larger rock) letting it dry between applications. Finish by applying two thin coats of Dominator Wet Look Paver Sealer to your pavers, backrolling any excess. Ornamental grasses do particularly well in the Northeast because many varieties are naturally adapted to cold winters, seasonal changes, and a wide range of soil conditions. Their deep, extensive root systems help them tolerate periods of summer heat and drought once established, while their dormant crowns allow them to survive freezing temperatures and return reliably each spring. Many grasses also thrive in the Northeast’s full sun and well-drained soils and require relatively little maintenance compared with many flowering plants. Their ability to handle both the cold winters and humid summers makes them a dependable choice for Northeast landscapes, while their movement, texture, and winter interest add structure to the landscape year-round.#Westchester#westchestercounty #planting #landscapedesign #Greenwich
